rows.en: The coals aren't going to light themselves.
rows.draft: Mashala ha a na ho itukisa ka bo 'ona.
rows.reason: itukisa is an odd reflexive that reads close to itokisa (prepare oneself), and 'ha a na ho' is stiff; a speaker would say the coals won't catch by themselves: a ke ke a tuka.
rows.rewrite: Mashala a ke ke a tuka ka bo ona.

rows.en: Absolutely beautiful out there.
rows.draft: Ho motle haholo kantle.
rows.reason: motle is for a person and does not agree with ho; weather beauty is hotle (ho hotle).
rows.rewrite: Ho hotle haholo kantle.

rows.en: Beach or braai? Yes.
rows.draft: Lebopo kapa braai? E.
rows.reason: Short either/or with the one-word 'E.' turn lands exactly as in English; lebopo (shore) carries the beach.

rows.en: Fog so thick it has opinions.
rows.draft: Moholi o mokoto haholo o na le maikutlo.
rows.reason: mokoto is thickness of a solid (a stick), not of fog, and without hoo (so...that) the two clauses are jammed together.
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o mongata hoo o seng o na le maikutlo.

rows.en: Even the hadedas sound happy.
rows.draft: Esita le dinonyana di utloahala li thabile.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; dinonyana for hadedas is how the natives rendered it before (di/li mixing is only spelling), though the loud-hadeda irony goes a little flat.

rows.en: Overcast but we'll survive.
rows.draft: Ho na le maru empa re tla phela.
rows.reason: Ho na le maru plus the everyday 're tla phela' gives the same shrugging survival as the English.

rows.en: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.
rows.draft: Lipara tse tharo tsa dikausu empa ha li ea lekana.
rows.reason: Lipara is a shaky loan where speakers would just code-switch di-pair, and 'still' is dropped, which blunts the turn.
rows.rewrite: Di-pair tse tharo tsa dikausu, empa le jwale ha di a lekana.

rows.en: Warm one coming, give or take a few degrees.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le futhumetseng le tla, mohlomong.
rows.reason: Sentence-final verb wants the long form le a tla, and mohlomong hedges whether it will be warm at all rather than the exact degrees.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le futhumetseng le a tla — dikgerata tsona, hoo e ka bang.

rows.en: Windows closed, kettle on, and wait.
rows.draft: Lifensetere li koetsoe, ketlele e butsoe, ema.
rows.reason: ketlele e butsoe reads as the kettle's lid is open, not boiling (natives use bedisa ketlele), and bare ema (stand/stop) is what natives replaced with dula for waiting out a storm.
rows.rewrite: Kwala difensetere, bedisa ketlele, o dule o emetse.

rows.en: The commute just became a team sport.
rows.draft: Leeto le fetohile papali ea sehlopha.
rows.reason: Leeto alone is any trip, so the commute is lost; 'just became' is le sa tswa fetoha in the natives' lines.
rows.rewrite: Leeto la ho ya mosebetsing le sa tswa fetoha papadi ya sehlopha.

rows.en: The sky just went full Carte Blanche.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le fetohile Carte Blanche ka botlalo.
rows.reason: Carte Blanche reference kept as natives kept it before, and ka botlalo matches their own 'le halefile ka botlalo'.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.draft: Moholi o jele tikoloho.
rows.reason: o jele (has eaten) keeps the personified fog swallowing the area; short and natural.

rows.en: The car's heater is the most important relationship in your life right now.
rows.draft: Heater ya koloi ke relationship ya bohlokwa ka ho fetisisa bophelong ba hao hona jwale.
rows.reason: Urban code-switch (heater, relationship) the way people actually talk, with correct ka ho fetisisa / bophelong ba hao frame.

rows.en: Everything looks 4K today. The sky's in ultra mode.
rows.draft: Tsohle li shebahala 4K kajeno. Lehodimo le ultra mode.
rows.reason: Lehodimo le ultra mode lacks the locative the natives used ('di ho max'), and shebahala wants jwalo ka before 4K.
rows.rewrite: Tsohle di shebahala jwalo ka 4K kajeno. Lehodimo le ho ultra mode.

rows.en: Weather's being more indecisive than you at Spur.
rows.draft: Leholimo ha le tsebe ho iketsa joalo ka uena Spur.
rows.reason: iketsa means to make oneself/pretend, not to decide, and 'joalo ka uena' says 'like you' not 'more than you' — the line no longer says the sky is indecisive.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le thatafallwa ke ho etsa qeto ho feta wena ha o le Spur.

rows.en: Nothing to see here. Literally.
rows.draft: Ha ho letho leo ho le bonoang mona. Ka nnete.
rows.reason: 'leo ho le bonoang' is a tangled passive relative; natives say 'le bonahalang' (Ha ho leru le bonahalang).
rows.rewrite: Ha ho letho le bonahalang mona. Ka nnete.

rows.en: Probably a scorcher. A hat's not a bad idea.
rows.draft: Mohlomong letsatsi le chesang. Katiba hase mohopolo o mobe.
rows.reason: Same Mohlomong-letsatsi-le-X shape the natives kept in the low-confidence lines; the hat advice reads easy and dry.

rows.en: Stay safe. The sky is making a point.
rows.draft: Lula u bolokehile. Lehodimo le etsa ntlha.
rows.reason: etsa ntlha is a calque of 'make a point' (ntlha = a dot/point), not something said of a stormy sky.
rows.rewrite: Dula o bolokehile. Lehodimo le na le seo le se bolelang.

rows.en: The couch has made a compelling case for staying.
rows.draft: Sofa e entsoe nyeoe e matla ea ho dula.
rows.reason: e entsoe is passive (the couch was made), and nyeoe is a court case, so it reads as the sofa being turned into a lawsuit.
rows.rewrite: Sofa e o kgodisitse hore o dule.

rows.en: Perfect conditions for losing your dignity.
rows.draft: Maemo a phethahetseng a ho lahleheloa ke seriti.
rows.reason: Maemo a phethahetseng is bureaucratic; natives frame 'perfect weather for' as Lehodimo le loketseng ho; lahlehelwa ke seriti is right.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le loketseng ho lahlehelwa ke seriti.

rows.en: Quiet out there. Almost suspicious.
rows.draft: Ho kgutsitse kantle. E batla ho belaela.
rows.reason: batla + infinitive (batla ho) means 'wants to', so 'E batla ho belaela' says 'it wants to suspect'; almost is batla + participle (E batla e le).
rows.rewrite: Ho kgutsitse kantle. E batla e belaetsa.

rows.en: Don't even think about driving somewhere.
rows.draft: Se ke oa nahana ho otlela kae kapa kae.
rows.reason: 'even' is dropped (needs le ho), and natives changed otlela to kganna for driving.
rows.rewrite: O se ke wa nahana le ho kganna ho ya kae kapa kae.

rows.en: Table Mountain? What Table Mountain?
rows.draft: Table Mountain? Table Mountain efe?
rows.reason: 'Table Mountain efe?' is the natural Sesotho 'which one?' with the right class-9 concord; the deadpan lands intact.

rows.en: Good enough weather. Not great, not terrible.
rows.draft: Leholimo le lekaneng. Ha le leholo, ha le lebe.
rows.reason: 'Ha le leholo' means 'it is not big', not 'not great'; 'leholimo le lekaneng' is stiff. Speakers say 'ha ho monate haholo, ha ho mpe'.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le lokile feela. Ha ho monate haholo, empa ha ho mpe.

rows.en: The type of day that makes people text 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.draft: Mofuta oa letsatsi o etsang batho ba romele 'letsatsi le letle hey'.
rows.reason: 'o etsang batho ba romele' is missing 'hore' (the corpus says 'o etsang hore ...'), and 'romele' without an object reads unfinished.
rows.rewrite: Mofuta wa letsatsi o etsang hore batho ba romelane 'letsatsi le letle hey'.

rows.en: Your washing just moved to the neighbour's yard.
rows.draft: Liaparo tsa hao li sa tsoa fallela jareteng ea moahisane.
rows.reason: 'fallela' (moved house to) makes the washing a tenant who relocated, which is a natural, funny image. 'jareteng' for 'jarateng' is a small spelling variant only.

rows.en: The kind of day Joburg pretends it doesn't have until you're standing in it.
rows.draft: Letsatsi la mofuta oo Joburg e iketsang eka ha e na lona, ho fihlela o eme ka hara lona.
rows.reason: The agreement is mixed ('oo' agrees with mofuta, 'lona' with letsatsi), and 'o eme ka hara lona' (standing inside a day) is a translated image. A speaker says 'until you step outside'.
rows.rewrite: Mofuta wa letsatsi oo Joburg e iketsang eka ha e na wona, ho fihlela o tswela kantle.

rows.en: Eskom-friendly weather. No solar today.
rows.draft: Leholimo le ratoang ke Eskom. Ha ho solar kajeno.
rows.reason: 'le ratwang ke Eskom' plus code-switched 'solar' reads like real speech; the no-sun/grid joke carries.

rows.en: The duvet had the right idea this morning.
rows.draft: Duvet e ne e na le mohopolo o nepahetseng hoseng.
rows.reason: 'e ne e na le mohopolo o nepahetseng' is a word-for-word calque of 'had the right idea'. A speaker says 'e ne e nepile' (it was right), and 'this morning' needs 'hoseng hona'.
rows.rewrite: Duvet e ne e nepile hoseng hona.

rows.en: Three hadedas, two crows, one shivering human at the bird feeder.
rows.draft: Hadedas tse tharo, crows tse pedi, human a le mong ya thothomelang ho bird feeder.
rows.reason: This is an English list with Sesotho glue ('crows', 'human a le mong', 'bird feeder'), the same fault as the CUT frost anchor. 'human' takes motho, and crows are makgwaba.
rows.rewrite: Di-hadeda tse tharo, makgwaba a mabedi, le motho a le mong ya thothomelang moo dinonyana di jang teng.

rows.en: Days like this is why we put up with the load shedding.
rows.draft: Matsatsi a tjena ke lebaka leo re mametseng load shedding.
rows.reason: 're mametseng' comes from mamela (listen), so it says 'we listened to load shedding', not 'endure' (mamella). 'lebaka leo re ...' also lacks 'ka lona'.
rows.rewrite: Matsatsi a tjena ke ona a etsang hore re mamelle load shedding.

rows.en: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.
rows.draft: Nka motsotso. Sheba holimo. Kea leboha.
rows.reason: 'Kea leboha' means 'thank you', not 'you're welcome', so the app thanks the reader and the smug brag flips. 'Nka motsotso' is also a calque.
rows.rewrite: Ema hanyane. Sheba hodimo. O ka re leboha hamorao.

rows.en: Could go misty. The dew point's flirting with it.
rows.draft: Ho ka ba le mohodi. Ela hloko.
rows.reason: It is natural, but 'Ela hloko' (be careful) swaps the joke for a flat warning; the dew-point flirting turn is gone.
rows.rewrite: Ho ka ba le mohodi. Lehodimo le ntse le o mema.

rows.en: You miss your bed and you've been gone twelve minutes.
rows.draft: O hopola bethe ea hao mme o tsoile metsotso e leshome le metso e 'meli.
rows.reason: 'hopola' means remember, not miss (hlolohelwa). The spelled-out 'e leshome le metso e 'meli' is heavy, and the punch needs 'feela'.
rows.rewrite: O se o hlolohetswe bethe ya hao, mme o tswile metsotso e 12 feela.

rows.en: Fog might be rolling in. Keep an eye on the mountain.
rows.draft: Mohodi o ka kena. Sheba thaba.
rows.reason: 'kena' (enter) is odd for fog arriving, where a speaker says 'fihla' or 'tla'. 'keep an eye on' is 'dula o shebile', as in the corpus.
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o ka fihla. Dula o shebile thaba.

rows.en: Marinade in. Phone off. Day starts now.
rows.draft: Kenya marinade. Tima mohala. Letsatsi le qala joale.
rows.reason: 'Kenya marinade' has no meat in it and reads first as the country Kenya. The meat goes into the marinade, and people say 'founu'.
rows.rewrite: Kenya nama ka hara marinade. Tima founu. Letsatsi le qala jwale.

rows.en: Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.
rows.draft: Ntho e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe e lokolohileng serapaneng e khethile pefo.
rows.reason: 'e kgethile pefo' carries 'chose violence' the way the corpus keeps internet idioms; 'e lokolohileng' for loose things is understood.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.draft: Chesa Weber. Ke molao.
rows.reason: Transitive 'chesa' means burn the thing itself, so 'Chesa Weber' reads as 'set the Weber on fire'. To fire it up is 'hotetsa'.
rows.rewrite: Hotetsa Weber. Ke molao.

rows.en: The streetlights are trying their best.
rows.draft: Mabone a seterata a leka ka hohle.
rows.reason: 'Mabone a seterata a leka ka hohle' is natural, and the streetlights get a warm, struggling personality.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.draft: Ho bata ho lekana le soupa. Le soupa ea bobeli.
rows.reason: 'soupa' is the loan natives corrected to 'sopho', and 'ho lekana le soupa' says 'cold equal to soup'. A speaker says 'ho bata hoo ...'.
rows.rewrite: Ho bata hoo o hlokang sopho. Le sopho ya bobedi.

rows.en: The fog drank the mountain.
rows.draft: Moholi o noele thaba.
rows.reason: 'o noele' (drank) is a strange verb for fog; in Sesotho a thing that vanishes is swallowed ('metsa'), which keeps the image.
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o meditse thaba.

rows.en: If you're inside, you're doing it wrong.
rows.draft: Haeba o ka hare, o etsa phoso.
rows.reason: 'Haeba o ka hare, o etsa phoso' is plain, natural and carries the cheeky nudge outside.

rows.en: Kuier weather. Get the people together.
rows.draft: Leholimo la ho kopana. Bokella batho.
rows.reason: 'Bokella' is used for collecting things and money, so 'bokella batho' reads like rounding people up. Kuier is visiting, 'ho etelana', and a speaker would 'bitsa metswalle'.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo la ho etelana. Bitsa metswalle.

rows.en: Your suede shoes chose today? Bold.
rows.draft: Lieta tsa hao tsa suede li khethile kajeno? Sebete.
rows.reason: Shoes that 'chose today' are a natural personification, and the one-word 'Sebete.' gives a dry second beat.

rows.en: Good day for a walk, bad day for a tan.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le letle la ho tsamaea, le lebe la ho tjhesa.
rows.reason: 'ho tjhesa' means to be hot or to burn, not to tan, so it reads 'bad day for heat'. Code-switch the verb the way natives did with 'post-a'.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le letle la ho tsamaya, le lebe la ho tan-a.

rows.en: Nature just reminded us of the pecking order.
rows.draft: Tlhaho e sa tsoa re hopotsa hore na ke mang ea pele.
rows.reason: Natural; 'ke mang ea pele' carries the pecking order as who comes first, and Tlhaho as the boss works like the native-kept Tlhaho lines.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.draft: Bosiu bo motle ba ho bona Tsela ea Lebese.
rows.reason: 'Tsela ea Lebese' is the known calque for the Milky Way (it is Molalatladi), and 'bo motle' is wrong: motle is person agreement, a night is 'bo botle' or 'bo loketseng'.
rows.rewrite: Bosiu bo loketseng ho bona Molalatladi ka nnete.

rows.en: Sand in places sand should never be.
rows.draft: Lehlabathe libakeng tseo lehlabathe le sa lokelang ho ba teng.
rows.reason: Literal but natural, like the native-kept ponytail line; repeating lehlabathe keeps the rueful wink.

rows.en: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho's exporting it for free.
rows.draft: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho e a e exporta mahala.
rows.reason: 'Maluti-frost morning' leaves the content word frost in English (natives replaced frost with serame), and 'e a e exporta' is a forced loan; a speaker says Lesotho sends it to us.
rows.rewrite: Serame sa Maluti hoseng hona. Lesotho e re romella sona mahala.

rows.en: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.
rows.draft: Mohlomong sebakeng se seng estate agent e re 'lifestyle'.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong sebakeng se seng' is wordy and adds 'maybe' (somewhere is kae-kae), and 'estate agent e re' uses thing agreement for a person; it should be 'o re'.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae estate agent o re 'lifestyle'.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.draft: Digwagwa di kene puisanong.
rows.reason: Digwagwa is right for frogs, and the croaking read as joining the conversation carries the meme in Sesotho.

rows.en: Could get gusty. The forecast's a bit loose on this one.
rows.draft: Ho ka ba le moea. Ponelopele e hlephile mona.
rows.reason: 'Hlephile' is physical looseness (a slack rope or screw) and is odd for a forecast; a speaker says it has no certainty. 'Moea' alone also loses the gusts.
rows.rewrite: Moya o ka foka ka matla. Ponelopele ha e na bonnete ka taba ena.

rows.en: The aircon remote is now public property. Negotiate.
rows.draft: Remote ea aircon joale ke thepa ea sechaba. Buisana.
rows.reason: 'Thepa ea sechaba' is the everyday term for public property, and the one-word 'Buisana' lands the deadpan order.

rows.en: Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
rows.draft: Lekker koud, empa di-rugby fields di se di tlo shebahala perfect.
rows.reason: Urban code-switching of the kind natives kept (di-koppies, 'Cold ya mofuta'); the Sesotho frame is sound and 'lekker koud' is house voice.

rows.en: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.
rows.draft: Hona ha se seo brosure ea bohahlauli e neng e se tšepisa.
rows.reason: Clean and natural; 'brosure' matches the native-kept brochure line, and bohahlauli is the right word for tourism.

rows.en: Wet jeans for the rest of the day. The classic punishment.
rows.draft: Lijinse tse metsi letsatsi lohle. Kotlo ea setso.
rows.reason: It mirrors the native-kept 'Dikausu tse metsi' shape, and natives let 'Setso' stand for classic, so 'Kotlo ea setso' reads as the wry usual punishment.

rows.en: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. Moment of silence.
rows.draft: Kae-kae sekhele se sa tsoa reteleha ka hare. Motsotso oa kgutso.
rows.reason: 'Reteleha ka hare' means turned inward or around, not inside out; for an umbrella blown over a speaker says 'phethoha'. 'Motsotso oa kgutso' is right.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae sekhele se sa tswa phethoha ke moya. Motsotso wa kgutso.

rows.en: Thunder's grumbling, hey.
rows.draft: Ledimo le a duma.
rows.reason: 'Ledimo' is a cannibal or ogre in Sesotho, so the line says a cannibal is rumbling; thunder is 'lehodimo le a duma' or seaduma. The 'hey' is lost too.
rows.rewrite: Eish, lehodimo le a duma.

rows.en: The southeaster's arrived. Uninvited, as usual.
rows.draft: Moea oa boroa o fihlile. O sa mengoa, joalo ka kamehla.
rows.reason: 'Moea oa boroa' is the south wind; the Cape Southeaster stays as the loan, as the house does. 'O sa mengoa, joalo ka kamehla' is good and lands the joke.
rows.rewrite: Southeaster e fihlile. E sa mengwa, jwalo ka kamehla.

rows.en: A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le karolelano le etsang lintho tsa karolelano.
rows.reason: 'Lehodimo le karolelano le etsang' is garbled: it reads 'the sky is an average which does', and dropping 'perfectly' loses the deadpan repetition. It needs the possessive 'la karolelano'.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo la karolelano feela, le etsa dintho tsa karolelano feela.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.draft: Dinaledi di teng, load shedding e ke ke ea ama sena.
rows.reason: Grammatical and clear; 'e ke ke ea ama sena' carries 'can't touch this', and the stars against load shedding comes through.

rows.en: The potholes are becoming swimming pools.
rows.draft: Mesima e fetoha matamo a ho sesa.
rows.reason: 'Mesima' for the holes and 'matamo a ho sesa' for swimming pools are plain and natural, and the turn from hole to pool lands.

rows.en: Grey skies, low conviction.
rows.draft: Leholimo le lerootho, tumelo e tlase.
rows.reason: 'Tumelo' is religious faith, so 'tumelo e tlase' reads as low faith; conviction here is certainty (bonnete, as in the confirmed lines).
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le lerootho, bonnete bo tlase.

rows.en: The neighbourhood cats have taken over.
rows.draft: Dikatse tsa moahisane di nkile taolo.
rows.reason: 'Tsa moahisane' is one neighbour's cats, not the neighbourhood's; it should be the plural baahisane. 'Di nkile taolo' is natural.
rows.rewrite: Dikatse tsa baahisane di nkile taolo.

rows.en: Tile floors are tonight's villain. Wear something on your feet.
rows.draft: Tile floors ke villain ya bosiu bona. Apara ntho maotong.
rows.reason: 'Tile floors ke villain' leaves both content nouns in English, the fault natives CUT in the frost line. Keep di-tiles as the loan and use sera (enemy) for villain. 'Apara ntho maotong' is good.
rows.rewrite: Di-tiles ke sera sa bosiu bona. Apara ntho maotong.

rows.en: If you can read this, you're too close.
rows.draft: Haeba o ka bala sena, o haufi haholo.
rows.reason: Clean, natural Sesotho, and the tailgating gag reads straight in fog.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.draft: Fynbos e e rata. Le uena o lokela.
rows.reason: 'Le uena o lokela' hangs without a verb (lokela needs 'ho ...'), and the object of 'e e rata' is vague; the native-kept garden line uses thabile/thaba for this turn.
rows.rewrite: Fynbos e thabile. Le wena o lokela ho thaba.

rows.en: The braai is the social calendar. Show up.
rows.draft: Braai ke khalendara ea boithabiso. Hlaha.
rows.reason: 'Khalendara ea boithabiso' is an entertainment calendar, not a social one, and 'Hlaha' (appear, come out) is stiff for 'show up'; a speaker says come and don't be left out.
rows.rewrite: Braai ke yona khalendara ya metswalle. Tla, o se ke wa sala.

rows.en: Your iced coffee melted before you reached the car.
rows.draft: Kofi ea hao ea leqhoa e qhibilihile pele o fihla koloing.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; 'kofi ya leqhwa e qhibilihile pele o fihla koloing' carries the heat joke without strain.

rows.en: The neighbours' pool has never looked so tempting.
rows.draft: Pool ea baahisane ha e e-s'o shebahale e khahlisang hakana.
rows.reason: Stiff: relative 'e khahlisang' after shebahala and 'ha e e-s'o' read translated; a speaker says 'ha e so ka e shebahala e le ...'.
rows.rewrite: Pool ya baahisane ha e so ka e shebahala e le monate hakana.

rows.en: The world ends two metres past the gate.
rows.draft: Lefatše le qetella limithara tse peli ka mose ho heke.
rows.reason: 'qetella' is ending in time (to finish); for where the world stops, a speaker says 'le fella'.
rows.rewrite: Lefatshe le fella dimithara tse pedi ka mose ho heke.

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.
rows.draft: Apara liaparo tse ngata joalo ka ho palama Sani Pass.
rows.reason: 'jwalo ka ho palama' is translated: palama is board/ride and the comparison has no 'you'; a speaker says 'eka o nyoloha'.
rows.rewrite: Apara diaparo tse ngata, eka o nyoloha Sani Pass.

rows.en: Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.
rows.draft: Tsohle li shebahala joalo ka filimi. E tšosang.
rows.reason: Two beats with the turn intact; 'E tshosang.' works as a dry elliptical 'a scary one'.

rows.en: It is what it is.
rows.draft: Ke seo e leng sona.
rows.reason: 'Ke seo e leng sona' is a word-for-word calque of the English idiom; the Sesotho shrug is 'ke kamoo ho leng ka teng'.
rows.rewrite: Ke kamoo ho leng ka teng.

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.draft: Welkom-cold kajeno. Serame se fetang ka di-jersey tse tharo jwalo ka ha di se teng.
rows.reason: 'jwalo ka ha di se teng' reads as 'since they are not there'; 'as if' is eka, as the natives write it. Welkom-cold code-switch is fine.
rows.rewrite: Welkom-cold kajeno. Serame se fetang ka hara di-jersey tse tharo eka ha di teng.

rows.en: The garden's saying dankie at last.
rows.draft: Jarata e re kea leboha qetellong.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; jarata and qetellong are the natives' own words, 'e re ke a leboha' gives the garden a voice.

rows.en: Nature's having a word. Best to listen.
rows.draft: Tlhaho e batla ho bua. Ho molemo ho mametsa.
rows.reason: Tlhaho as a character that wants a word, then the dry advice; reads naturally.

rows.en: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.
rows.draft: Mohlomong pula, mohlomong che. Setso.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong pula, mohlomong tjhe' is how people say it; 'Setso' for Classic matches the natives' confirmed usage.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le tjhabile. O se ke wa thetswa. Nature e bua leshano.
rows.reason: 'Nature' is forced English where Sesotho has tlhaho (the word the natives use); the rest is natural.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le tjhabile. O se ke wa thetswa. Tlhaho e bua leshano.

rows.en: The dog is still keen. The dog is always keen. Respect.
rows.draft: Ntja e ntse e le keen. Ntja e dula e le keen. Respect.
rows.reason: 'keen' and 'Respect' are raw English where people say mafolofolo and hlompha (natives replaced 'Respect' with Hlompha); the repeat structure is good.
rows.rewrite: Ntja e ntse e le mafolofolo. Ntja e dula e le mafolofolo. Re a e hlompha.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.draft: Mathata a tšepo le lehodimo kajeno.
rows.reason: 'Mathata a tshepo le lehodimo' is a calque of 'trust issues' and tshepo also reads as 'hope'; a speaker would just say they don't trust the sky.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo la kajeno? Ha ke le tshepe.

rows.en: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.
rows.draft: Beha lena ka botlolong. Bula nakong ea mariha.
rows.reason: 'Bula' needs the object (le bule) and 'beha ... ka botlolong' is stiff; into a bottle is kenya, and 'lena' alone leaves the day unnamed.
rows.rewrite: Kenya letsatsi lena ka botlolong. O le bule mariha.

rows.en: You will look like a lobster. You've been warned.
rows.draft: O tla shebahala joalo ka lobster. O lemoselitsoe.
rows.reason: 'O lemoselitsoe' is a malformed passive; 'you have been warned' is 'o lemositswe'. Lobster as a loan is fine.
rows.rewrite: O tla shebahala jwalo ka lobster. O lemositswe.

rows.en: Looks wet. The models are fairly sure, not certain.
rows.draft: Ho bonahala ho le metsi. Limodele li na le bonnete mohlomong, eseng ka botlalo.
rows.reason: 'Ho bonahala ho le metsi' and 'bonnete mohlomong' follow the natives' confirmed low-confidence lines; a plain remark that reads fine.

rows.en: The UV index is higher than your expectations.
rows.draft: UV index e phahameng ho feta litšepo tsa hao.
rows.reason: Relative 'e phahameng' leaves the sentence without a verb (same fault natives fixed in the sunscreen-budget line); should be 'e phahame'.
rows.rewrite: UV index e phahame ho feta ditshepo tsa hao.

rows.en: The fridge is the coolest room in the house.
rows.draft: Fridge ke kamore e pholileng ka ho fetisisa ka tlung.
rows.reason: Fridge as a loan is how people talk; 'kamore e pholileng ka ho fetisisa' lands the heat joke cleanly.

rows.en: Your hairstyle? Gone. Accept it.
rows.draft: Moriri oa hao? O ile. Amohela.
rows.reason: Three short beats that read naturally; 'O ile' for the hair and the bare imperative 'Amohela' carry the deadpan.

rows.en: The braai cover is in the next suburb.
rows.draft: Sekoahelo sa braai se seterekeng se latelang.
rows.reason: 'Sekoahelo sa braai' is the natives' own phrase; 'next district' keeps the blown-away hyperbole.

rows.en: The kids still going to school in shorts. They know things we don't.
rows.draft: Bana ba ntse ba ya school ka shorts. Ba tseba dintho tseo rona re sa di tsebeng.
rows.reason: 'ba ya school' leaves English where everyone says sekolong, and 'ka shorts' should be 'ba apere shorts'; second beat is natural.
rows.rewrite: Bana ba ntse ba ya sekolong ba apere shorts. Ba tseba dintho tseo rona re sa di tsebeng.

rows.en: Cancel everything. Even your excuses.
rows.draft: Hlakola tsohle. Esita le mabaka a hao.
rows.reason: 'Hlakola tsohle. Esita le mabaka a hao.' uses the natives' own hlakola, esita le, mabaka; two beats with the turn.

rows.en: Water consumption: yes. All of it.
rows.draft: Ho noa metsi: e. Kaofela.
rows.reason: Plain and natural: 'drinking water: yes. All of it.' keeps the dry two-beat shape; kaofela carries 'all of it'.

rows.en: Postcard weather. You're welcome.
rows.draft: Leholimo la postcard. Kea leboha.
rows.reason: 'Kea leboha' means 'thank you', not 'you're welcome', so the smug credit-taking turns into the app thanking the reader; the first beat (postcard code-switch) is fine.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo la postcard. Ke mpho e tswang ho rona.

rows.en: Somewhere a roof is someone's new kite.
rows.draft: Mohlomong sebakeng se seng marulelo ke khaete e ncha.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong' means 'maybe', not 'somewhere' (the corpus uses kae-kae); 'someone's' is dropped, and 'khaete' is forced where people just say kite.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae, marulelo a motho e mong jwale ke kite ya hae e ntjha.

rows.en: Cape Town just got a dimmer switch.
rows.draft: Cape Town e fumane konopo ea ho fokotsa lesedi.
rows.reason: 'konopo ea ho fokotsa lesedi' is a literal description of a dimmer switch and reads translated, and 'just' is lost; a speaker would say someone just turned Cape Town's light down.
rows.rewrite: Motho e mong o sa tswa fokotsa lesedi la Cape Town.

rows.en: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.
rows.draft: Mohlomong pula, mohlomong che. Tloaelo.
rows.reason: Natural hedge, matching the kept 'mohlomong pula' and 'kapa mohlomong tjhe'; 'Tloaelo.' stands as the bare-noun 'Classic', like the kept 'Setso.'.

rows.en: Lightning's putting Eskom's grid to shame.
rows.draft: Lehadima le hlabisa Eskom dihlong.
rows.reason: 'hlabisa dihlong' is the real idiom for putting to shame; 'grid' drops out but the joke about Eskom being shamed comes through.

rows.en: Somewhere between fine and soaked. Good luck.
rows.draft: Pakeng tsa ho loka le ho ba metsi. Katleho.
rows.reason: Understood and natural; 'metsi' for wet matches the kept 'maemo a metsi', and 'Katleho' for good luck is confirmed. It is a little flatter than 'soaked'.

rows.en: Might spit a bit. Might not bother.
rows.draft: Ho ka tšela hanyane. Ho ka se tshoenyehe.
rows.reason: 'tšela' means pour, which clashes with 'a bit', and 'tshoenyehe' means 'be worried', not 'bother'. Read together, the line says 'might not be worried'.
rows.rewrite: Pula e ka na hanyane. Kapa e ka se itshwenye.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.draft: Leholimo le letle la soupa.
rows.reason: 'soupa' is the known raw loan, and the word is sopho; the 'not gonna lie' turn is dropped, and 'ka nnete' gives it back.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le letle la sopho, ka nnete.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.draft: Maru a arabile 'mohlomong' empa a fihlile.
rows.reason: 'answered maybe but arrived anyway' reads naturally, and the clouds-as-guests joke lands without the RSVP loan.

rows.en: Coffee in the sun on the stoep. The whole reason we live here.
rows.draft: Coffee letsatsing stoepong. Ke lona lebaka lohle leo re dulang mona.
rows.reason: 'Coffee' is left raw where natives write kofi, and 'lebaka lohle leo re dulang mona' lacks 'ka lona'; the confirmed 'Ke kahoo re dulang...' is the natural shape.
rows.rewrite: Kofi letsatsing stoepong. Ke kahoo re dulang mona.

rows.en: Not the time for hero moves, hey.
rows.draft: Ha se nako ea bosenatla, hey.
rows.reason: 'bosenatla' (heroics) is exactly right, and the code-switched 'hey' is how people talk.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.draft: Lebaka le letle la ho hlakola merero.
rows.reason: Natural: 'lebaka le letle' plus 'hlakola merero' matches the confirmed 'e hlakotswe' usage.

rows.en: The bins are on an adventure again.
rows.draft: Matlakala a tsamaisong hape.
rows.reason: 'tsamaisong' means 'in administration/management', not 'on an adventure/trip' (leetong), and 'matlakala' is rubbish, not the bins.
rows.rewrite: Di-bin di leetong hape.

rows.en: Probably a bit of cloud. Or a lot. Hard to call.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho na le maru a manyane. Kapa a mangata. Ho thata ho bolela.
rows.reason: Reads like speech: 'maru a manyane... kapa a mangata. Ho thata ho bolela', in the same register as the kept low-confidence lines.

rows.en: The sky's giving mixed signals again.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le fana le matšoao a tsoakaneng hape.
rows.reason: 'matšoao a tsoakaneng' carries 'mixed signals' clearly, and 'fana le' mirrors the native-kept 'Lehodimo le fana le tsohle'.

rows.en: Eskom wishes it had this power.
rows.draft: Eskom e ka rata matla ana.
rows.reason: 'e ka rata matla ana' (would love this power) carries Eskom's envy simply and naturally.

rows.en: Not depressing. Just... underwhelming.
rows.draft: Ha ho masoabi. Feela... ha ho khotsofatse.
rows.reason: Sentence-initial 'Feela...' copies the English 'Just...' word order, and 'ha ho khotsofatse' (not satisfying) is stiff; 'not impressive' with feela at the end is how it is said.
rows.rewrite: Ha ho maswabi. Ha ho kgahlise feela.

rows.en: Cape Town's twinkling. Probably.
rows.draft: Cape Town e phatsima. Mohlomong.
rows.reason: 'phatsima' is the right sparkle word, and the dry 'Mohlomong.' tag works as the app's own hedge.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.draft: Grimase ea hao e na le nako ea ho fela ea 9 hoseng.
rows.reason: 'Grimase' is not Sesotho for makeup (it reads as grimace; people just say make-up), and 'nako ea ho fela ea 9 hoseng' is clunky throughout, so the line needs rewriting.
rows.rewrite: Make-up ya hao e fela ka 9 hoseng.

rows.en: Looks warm. How warm is a moving target.
rows.draft: Ho bonahala ho futhumetse. Hore na ho futhumetse hakae ho a fetoha.
rows.reason: Natural and clear ('how warm it is keeps changing'); the moving-target image goes flat, but nothing is wrong.

rows.en: Even the weather apps are arguing about this one.
rows.draft: Esita le di-app tsa leholimo li phehisana ka sena.
rows.reason: 'di-app' is a natural code-switch, and 'phehisana' (argue with each other) is exactly the word.

rows.en: The fridge door is getting a workout today.
rows.draft: Monyako oa fridge o fumana boikoetliso kajeno.
rows.reason: 'o fumana boikoetliso' calques 'getting a workout' and reads like 'is receiving training'; a speaker would say the door is doing exercise.
rows.rewrite: Monyako wa fridge o etsa boikwetliso kajeno.

rows.en: Probably hot. We'll all find out together.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho chesa. Re tla fumana kaofela hammoho.
rows.reason: 'Re tla fumana kaofela hammoho' reads as 'we will get/find all together'; for 'find out' a speaker says 're tla bona' (we'll see).
rows.rewrite: Mohlomong ho tla tjhesa. Re tla bona kaofela hammoho.

rows.en: Could be worse. Could also be better.
rows.draft: E ka ba mpe le ho feta. E ka ba betere le ho feta.
rows.reason: Weather takes the 'ho' subject (as in the confirmed 'Ha ho mpe, ha ho motle'), not 'e'; and 'betere' is a forced loan where 'hotle' is the house word for good weather.
rows.rewrite: Ho ka ba mpe le ho feta. Ho ka ba hotle le ho feta.

rows.en: Cloud cover with a side of who-cares.
rows.draft: Maru le lehlakore la mang ea tsotellang.
rows.reason: 'lehlakore' is a physical side; 'Maru le lehlakore la mang ea tsotellang' calques 'a side of' into 'clouds and the side of who cares' and makes no sense.
rows.rewrite: Maru a teng, empa ha ho motho ya tsotellang.

rows.en: The hadedas are sleeping. Finally.
rows.draft: Dinonyana di robetse. Qetellong.
rows.reason: Natural; 'dinonyana' for hadedas is what the natives kept elsewhere, and 'Qetellong' carries the relief.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.draft: Kopano le bohle ba nang le seeta se le seng se metsi joale.
rows.reason: 'Kopano' means a meeting or union, not solidarity, so the line opens as 'a meeting with everyone...'; 'joale' alone is weak for 'right now' (hona jwale).
rows.rewrite: Re utlwela bohloko bohle ba nang le seeta se le seng se metsi hona jwale.

rows.en: The sky is buffering.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le a buffera.
rows.reason: Tech loan used the way people code-switch (like the confirmed 'le sa loadhella'); short and dry.

rows.en: Hot water bottle is the real MVP today.
rows.draft: Botlolo ea metsi a chesang ke mohale oa 'nete kajeno.
rows.reason: 'mohale oa 'nete' (real hero) is a good Sesotho swap for MVP; hot water bottle phrase is plain and clear.

rows.en: The sky's undecided. So are we.
rows.draft: Leholimo ha le qeta. Le rona.
rows.reason: 'qeta' means finish, not decide: 'ha le qeta' says the sky isn't finishing; undecided is 'ha le e-so etse qeto' (as in the confirmed partly-cloudy line).
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo ha le e-so etse qeto. Le rona.

rows.en: Not a hairstyle in sight. Just survivors.
rows.draft: Ha ho setaele sa moriri se bonahalang. Ba pholosehileng feela.
rows.reason: 'ba pholosehileng' leans to 'the saved' (rescued, even religious), not people who survived the wind; a speaker says 'ba pholohileng'.
rows.rewrite: Ha ho setaele sa moriri se bonahalang. Ke ba pholohileng feela.

rows.en: Thunder so close the walls shook. Respect.
rows.draft: Modumo o haufi mabota a thothomela. Hlompho.
rows.reason: No 'so...that' link ('hoo') and present tense where the walls already shook; bare 'Hlompho.' is a stiff noun where a speaker says 'Re a o hlompha'.
rows.rewrite: Modumo o ne o le haufi hoo mabota a ileng a thothomela. Re a o hlompha.

rows.en: Outside is a test of character. You're failing.
rows.draft: Kantle ke teko ea botho. O a hloleha.
rows.reason: Two clean beats, 'teko ea botho' reads as a character test and 'O a hloleha' lands the jab.

rows.en: Even the seagulls are walking today.
rows.draft: Esita le dikoekoe di tsamaea kajeno.
rows.reason: 'dikoekoe' is not a word I can confirm for seagulls (people just say seagull), and 'di tsamaea' alone reads 'they are leaving', so the grounded-by-wind joke needs 'ka maoto'.
rows.rewrite: Esita le di-seagull di tsamaya ka maoto kajeno.

rows.en: Shoes optional. Attitude mandatory.
rows.draft: Lieta li ka khethoa. Boitšoaro bo tlamehile.
rows.reason: 'li ka khethoa' (can be chosen) and 'bo tlamehile' are translated-sounding; a speaker sets 'needed / not needed' against each other.
rows.rewrite: Dieta ha di hlokahale. Boitshwaro bo a hlokahala.

rows.en: Flip-flops on tar was a mistake.
rows.draft: Lislipase ho tara e ne e le phoso.
rows.reason: 'ho tara' is 'to tar', not 'on the tar' (tareng), and the mistake is walking in them, which the line never says.
rows.rewrite: Ho tsamaya ka di-slip-slop tareng e ne e le phoso.

rows.en: Probably windy. The Cape Doctor keeps its own diary.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho na le moea. Cape Doctor e na le bukana ea eona.
rows.reason: 'bukana' is just a booklet, so 'keeps its own diary' (its own schedule) is lost; 'lenaneo' is the word natives used for schedule, and they render Cape Doctor as 'Ngaka ya Cape'.
rows.rewrite: Mohlomong ho na le moya. Ngaka ya Cape e na le lenaneo la yona.

rows.en: Storm on the cards, not yet confirmed. Stay sharp.
rows.draft: Sefefo se monyetleng, ha se e-s'o netefatsoe. Lula u falimehile.
rows.reason: 'se monyetleng' matches the natives' own 'Mohodi o monyetleng'; 'Lula u falimehile' is natural.

rows.en: Your future self will thank you for that sunscreen.
rows.draft: Uena oa hosane o tla leboha ka setofo sa letsatsi.
rows.reason: 'setofo' reads as stove (banned; sunscreen is 'setlolo sa letsatsi'), and 'o tla leboha' lacks the object 'you' (o tla o leboha).
rows.rewrite: Wena wa hosane o tla o leboha bakeng sa setlolo sa letsatsi.

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.draft: Hobaneng uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng o entse merero? Uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng o mobe.
rows.reason: 'uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng' is a hyphenated calque nobody says, twice over; a native would write a new line.
rows.rewrite: Hobaneng o ile wa etsa merero? Wena wa maobane o mobe ka ho fetisisa.

rows.en: This is the weather the weekend was invented for.
rows.draft: Lena ke leholimo phomolo e entsoeng bakeng sa lona.
rows.reason: Missing the relative 'leo' ('leholimo phomolo e entsoeng' doesn't parse), and 'phomolo' is rest/holiday, not the weekend (mafelo a beke).
rows.rewrite: Lena ke lehodimo leo mafelo a beke a entsweng bakeng sa lona.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.draft: Se ke oa tšepa maru ao. A rera.
rows.reason: Bare 'A rera' is clipped and can read 'they preach'; the natives' own idiom is 'a na le merero' (the river has plans).
rows.rewrite: Se ke wa tshepa maru ao. A na le merero.

rows.en: Schrodinger's rain. It both is and isn't.
rows.draft: Pula ea Schrödinger. E teng le ha e eo.
rows.reason: 'le ha e eo' can read 'even when it is there', blurring the is/isn't contradiction; say it with the rain verb itself.
rows.rewrite: Pula ya Schrödinger. E a na, e bile ha e ne.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.draft: Boloka letsatsi lena mohopolong.
rows.reason: 'Boloka letsatsi lena mohopolong' is a natural, warm Sesotho way to say it.

rows.en: Somewhere a cricket is really giving it.
rows.draft: Kae-kae tšie e binela ka matla.
rows.reason: 'tšie' is grasshopper, not cricket (tswiritswiri), and 'e binela' (sings for) is the wrong verb form; 'e bina ka matla'.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae tswiritswiri e bina ka matla.

rows.en: Your vitamin D levels are thanking you.
rows.draft: Maemo a hao a vitamin D a a leboha.
rows.reason: Natural: 'maemo' for levels matches the confirmed 'Boemo ba UV', 'a a leboha' reads as a speaker's thanks; vitamin D stays as the loan people use.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.
rows.draft: E, ke leholimo la jersey. Jersey tse peli.
rows.reason: 'Lehodimo la jersey' works (same pattern natives kept for shorts/underwear weather), but the plural loan needs its class prefix, as natives wrote 'Di-fleece tse pedi': 'Jersey tse peli' → 'Di-jersey tse pedi'.
rows.rewrite: E, ke lehodimo la jersey. Di-jersey tse pedi.

rows.en: The sun's on airplane mode.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le ho airplane mode.
rows.reason: Code-switch the way people talk ('le ho airplane mode' like the confirmed 'di ho max'); the sun-as-character joke lands.

rows.en: The dog's under the bed. Smart move, honestly.
rows.draft: Ntja e ka tlas'a bethe. Mohato o bohlale, ka nnete.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; 'Mohato o bohlale, ka nnete' carries the dry nod to the dog, same literal-but-clean register the natives kept.

rows.en: The ice cream van is playing everyone's anthem.
rows.draft: Bane ea ice cream e bapala pina ea bohle.
rows.reason: 'Bane' is not how people say van; just use the loan 'van'. 'Pina ya bohle' is fine for everyone's anthem.
rows.rewrite: Van ya ice cream e bapala pina ya bohle.

rows.en: The office aircon debate just went to level 5.
rows.draft: Puisano ea aircon ea ofisi e sa tsoa fihla boemong ba 5.
rows.reason: 'Puisano' is a calm discussion, not a heated debate — natives use 'kgang' for an argument; the stacked 'ea aircon ea ofisi' is stiff, a speaker says 'ofising'.
rows.rewrite: Kgang ya aircon ofising e se e fihlile level 5.

rows.en: The fog arrived unannounced. Classic fog.
rows.draft: Moholi o fihlile a sa memioa. Moholi oa setso.
rows.reason: Agreement slip: mohodi takes 'o', so 'a sa memioa' → 'o sa memwa'; 'Moholi oa setso' reads as 'traditional fog' — 'Classic' is better carried by 'Jwalo ka kamehla' (as always).
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o fihlile o sa memwa. Jwalo ka kamehla.

rows.en: Dark outside, bright tomorrow.
rows.draft: Ho fifala kantle, ho phatsima hosane.
rows.reason: Tense off: 'ho phatsima hosane' needs the future 'ho tla'; 'phatsima' is sparkle/glitter — for a bright day a speaker says 'kganya'.
rows.rewrite: Ho lefifi kantle, empa hosane ho tla kganya.

rows.en: Walking into it feels like a video game boss fight.
rows.draft: Ho tsamaea ho eona ho ikutloa joalo ka ntoa ea boss ea papali ea video.
rows.reason: Translated throughout: 'ho eona' agrees with nothing (wind is moya, class 3) so the reader never learns it is the wind; 'ho ikutloa' is to feel oneself, not 'it feels like'; the chain 'ntoa ea boss ea papali ea video' is stiff.
rows.rewrite: Ho tsamaya kgahlanong le moya ona ke ntwa le boss ya video game.

rows.en: The sky's reminding us who's boss.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le re hopotsa hore ke mang monga'a.
rows.reason: 'monga'a' (owner of) needs a noun after it and does not mean boss on its own; a speaker says 'ke mang ya laolang' (who's in charge).
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le re hopotsa hore ke mang ya laolang mona.

rows.en: No filter needed. Just look outside.
rows.draft: Ha ho hlokahale filitha. Sheba kantle feela.
rows.reason: Natural and short; the Instagram-filter joke comes through, 'Sheba kantle feela' makes clear which filter.

rows.en: Ice cream isn't a treat. It's survival.
rows.draft: Ice cream ha se mpho. Ke bophelo.
rows.reason: 'mpho' is a gift, not a treat; 'Ke bophelo' (it's life) works well. A speaker says it's not just something nice.
rows.rewrite: Ice cream hase ntho e monate feela. Ke bophelo.

rows.en: Hot-ish, likely. Keep the water close.
rows.draft: Ho chesa mohlomong. Boloka metsi haufi.
rows.reason: Plain, natural low-confidence line in the shape natives kept ('Ho a bata, mohlomong'); warm practical advice.

rows.en: The weekend doesn't get better than this.
rows.draft: Phomolo ha e be betere ho feta mona.
rows.reason: 'Phomolo' is rest/holiday, not weekend — natives use 'mafelo a beke'; 'betere' is a forced loan where 'monate' does the job; 'ho feta mona' is 'than here'.
rows.rewrite: Ha ho mafelo a beke a monate ho feta ana.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.draft: Pula e boima haholo e lokela ho lefa rente.
rows.reason: 'Pula e boima' calques heavy (boima = weighty/difficult); heavy rain is 'pula e matla', and 'so … that' needs 'hoo'.
rows.rewrite: Pula e matla hoo e lokelang ho lefa rente.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or don't. We're only fairly sure.
rows.draft: Nka baki. Kapa che. Re na le bonnete feela mohlomong.
rows.reason: 'Nka baki. Kapa tjhe.' is everyday speech; 'Re na le bonnete … mohlomong' is the hedge natives already kept for 'fairly sure'.

rows.en: Highveld winter: the only place where you wear two jackets to fetch the post.
rows.draft: Highveld winter: ke moo o aparang jackets tse pedi ho lata post.
rows.reason: English content words left raw: 'jackets' should be 'dijakete', 'winter' 'mariha', 'post' 'poso' (natives cut the English header in the kettle line); 'the only place' was dropped — add 'feela'.
rows.rewrite: Mariha a Highveld: ke feela moo o aparang dijakete tse pedi ho ya lata poso.

rows.en: Your shoes are about to have a bad day.
rows.draft: Lieta tsa hao li tla ba le letsatsi le lebe.
rows.reason: Grammatical and natural; shoes with feelings reads as easily as the confirmed duvet and dog lines.

rows.en: No alarm. No agenda. Just vibes.
rows.draft: Ha ho alarm. Ha ho agenda. Vibes feela.
rows.reason: Natives swap English content words for the everyday Sesotho one: 'agenda' → 'lenaneo' (their word for schedule); 'alarm' and 'vibes feela' stay as people say them.
rows.rewrite: Ha ho alarm. Ha ho lenaneo. Ke vibes feela.

rows.en: Somewhere a chocolate bar just died.
rows.draft: Mohlomong sebakeng se seng tšokolate e sa tsoa qhibiliha.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong sebakeng se seng' is stiff and adds a 'maybe' — natives say 'Kae-kae' for somewhere; 'e sa tswa qhibiliha' explains the joke instead of letting the chocolate die.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae, tšokolate e sa tswa qhibiliha ya shwa.

rows.en: Wind's on the cards. Peg the washing down.
rows.draft: Moea o monyetleng. Hokahanya liaparo tsa ho hlatsoa.
rows.reason: 'Moya o monyetleng' is good (natives kept 'Mohodi o monyetleng'), but 'hokahanya' means connect/coordinate, not peg down; 'diaparo tsa ho hlatswa' is clothes-to-be-washed, not the hung washing.
rows.rewrite: Moya o monyetleng. Tiisa diaparo tse fanyehilweng.

rows.en: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.
rows.draft: Ho tsamaisa ntja e fetohile papali ea tšepo.
rows.reason: Agreement off: the infinitive 'Ho tsamaisa' takes 'ho', not 'e' ('ho fetohile'); 'tlhahlobo' (test) carries trust exercise better than 'papali' (game).
rows.rewrite: Ho tsamaisa ntja ho fetohile tlhahlobo ya tshepo.

rows.en: Whoever has a pool today is your new best friend.
rows.draft: Mang kapa mang ea nang le pool kajeno ke motsoalle oa hao e mocha e moholo.
rows.reason: Stacking 'e mocha e moholo' reads 'new old/elder friend' side by side; 'motswalle e moholo' already carries best friend, let 'jwale' carry 'new'.
rows.rewrite: Mang kapa mang ya nang le pool kajeno ke motswalle wa hao e moholo jwale.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
rows.draft: Tšoara katiba ea hao! Le bana ba hao.
rows.reason: Plain everyday Sesotho, same two-beat turn as the English; 'Tshwara katiba' is what a speaker says.

rows.en: Pack an umbrella. Or don't. We don't know either.
rows.draft: Paka sekhele. Kapa o se ke oa paka. Ha re tsebe le rona.
rows.reason: Natural three beats; 'paka' is the accepted loan (cf. 'Paka ka nepo') and 'Ha re tsebe le rona' lands the shrug.

rows.en: Visibility sponsored by nobody.
rows.draft: Ho boneha ho sponsoritsoe ke motho. Motho.
rows.reason: 'ke motho. Motho.' means 'by a person. A person.' - it says somebody sponsors it, the opposite of 'nobody'; 'sponsoritsoe' is a forced loan.
rows.rewrite: Ho boneha kajeno: ha ho na sponsor.

rows.en: Breezy, probably. Maybe more.
rows.draft: Ho foka hanyane, mohlomong. Mohlomong ho feta.
rows.reason: Reads naturally; the repeated 'mohlomong' carries the hedge the way the kept 'Ponelopele e re mohlomong. Re re mohlomong.' does.

rows.en: Walking to the bin is now an expedition.
rows.draft: Ho tsamaea ho ea bining joale ke leeto.
rows.reason: Natural, same build as the kept 'Ho tsamaya ho ea koloing ke kotsi...'; 'leeto' (trip) is milder than 'expedition', so the hyperbole softens.

rows.en: Night looks calm. Models permitting.
rows.draft: Bosiu bo bonahala bo khutsitse. Haeba limodele li lumela.
rows.reason: 'Haeba dimodele di dumela' (if the models agree/consent) is a fair, natural carry of 'models permitting'.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.draft: Ho futhumetse ho lekane ho bula fensetere. O sebete?
rows.reason: 'ho futhumetse ho lekane ho bula' is the English 'warm enough to' calqued; and 'bula fensetere' is opening it, not leaving it open overnight, which is where the bravery is.
rows.rewrite: Ho futhumetse hoo o ka siyang fensetere e bulehile. Empa o na le sebete?

rows.en: Sky's throwing rocks. Stay inside.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le lahla majoe. Sala ka hare.
rows.reason: Sky throwing stones reads clearly as hail and 'Sala ka hare' matches the natives' own thunder line.

rows.en: Even your phone's overheating.
rows.draft: Esita le mohala oa hao o chesang.
rows.reason: 'o chesang' is a relative form ('your phone which is hot'), so the sentence has no main verb; a speaker says 'o tjhesa haholo'.
rows.rewrite: Esita le mohala wa hao o tjhesa haholo.

rows.en: The kind of day you text someone about.
rows.draft: Mofuta oa letsatsi oo o romelang motho molaetsa ka lona.
rows.reason: Agreement slip: 'oo' agrees with 'mofuta' but 'ka lona' points back to 'letsatsi'; the resumptive should be 'ka wona'.
rows.rewrite: Mofuta wa letsatsi oo o romelang motho molaetsa ka wona.

rows.en: Braai weather, boet! No excuses.
rows.draft: Leholimo la braai, boet! Ha ho mabaka.
rows.reason: 'Lehodimo la braai' follows the kept 'Lehodimo la Instagram' pattern; braai and boet stay as people say them; 'Ha ho mabaka' is a confirmed line.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le letala, moea o futhumetseng. Lintho tse bonolo.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; 'Lintho tse bonolo' leans 'easy things' rather than 'simple pleasures', so it reads a touch flat but not wrong.

rows.en: The office aircon war has begun.
rows.draft: Ntoa ea aircon ea ofisi e qalile.
rows.reason: Clean, with aircon and ofisi code-switched the way people say them; the office-war image survives.

rows.en: You could fry an egg on the N1.
rows.draft: O ka chesa lehe ho N1.
rows.reason: 'chesa lehe' is to burn an egg, not fry it - frying is 'hadika'; 'hodima N1' (on top of) reads better than 'ho N1', cf. the kept 'holim'a pavement'.
rows.rewrite: O ka hadika lehe hodima N1.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.draft: Tšebeliso ea rooibos e sa tsoa phethahala habeli.
rows.reason: 'Tshebediso ya rooibos' is report-speak and 'phethahala habeli' (be completed twice) is a calque of 'doubled'; a speaker talks about drinking it.
rows.rewrite: Ho nwa rooibos ho sa tswa eketseha habedi.

rows.en: Rain on the way, give or take.
rows.draft: Pula e tla, mohlomong.
rows.reason: Clause-final 'e tla' wants the 'a' ('e a tla', cf. 'Sefako se a tla'), otherwise it reads as the dangling future 'it will'; 'mohlomong' alone loses 'give or take'.
rows.rewrite: Pula e tseleng, plus minus.

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.draft: Esita le geyser e sebetsa lihora tse eketsehileng.
rows.reason: Natural; 'sebetsa dihora tse eketsehileng' matches the kept 'sebetsa nako e eketsehileng', and the geyser gets its personhood.

rows.en: Even the parking lot looks pretty today.
rows.draft: Esita le sebaka sa liphakinki se bonahala se setle kajeno.
rows.reason: 'se setle' is the right concord for 'sebaka' (not the person-only 'motle'); 'diphakinki' is a Sesotho-ised loan in the same vein as the kept 'Pavimente'.

rows.en: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.
rows.draft: Matsoho a hao a lipokothong 'me ha a tsoe.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; 'ha a tswe' carries the stubborn hands and the reader-tease lands.

rows.en: Storm's possible. The braai might need a rain check.
rows.draft: Sefefo se ka etsahala. Braai e ka hloka letsatsi le leng.
rows.reason: 'Braai e ka hloka letsatsi le leng' (might need another day) is a natural, idiomatic swap for 'rain check'.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.
rows.draft: Tšokolate e chesang ha se takatso. Ke tlhoko.
rows.reason: 'e tjhesang' for a hot drink is normal (like 'tee e tjhesang'); 'ha se takatso. Ke tlhoko.' is punchy and lands.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.draft: Ho boneha: hanyenyane nul.
rows.reason: 'hanyenyane nul' is 'very little' plus the Afrikaans 'nul' - garbled; a speaker says 'hoo e ka bang' (roughly) and just says 'zero'.
rows.rewrite: Ho boneha: hoo e ka bang zero.

rows.en: The sun doesn't care about your plans.
rows.draft: Letsatsi ha le khathalele merero ea hao.
rows.reason: Natural: same build as the confirmed 'Mohodi ha o khathalele lenaneo la hao'; the sun as an indifferent character lands.

rows.en: Tan lines are not a personality trait.
rows.draft: Mela ea ho tjhesa ha se botho.
rows.reason: 'Mela ea ho tjhesa' reads as burn lines, not tan lines, and bare 'ha se botho' reads 'is not humanity'; a speaker keeps 'tan lines' as the loan and says 'semelo sa hao' (your character).
rows.rewrite: Di-tan lines ha se semelo sa hao.

rows.en: Sky's looking moody. Could escalate.
rows.draft: Leholimo le bonahala le halefile. Ho ka eketseha.
rows.reason: 'Ho ka eketseha' (it could increase) leaves the reader asking what increases; 'escalate' is 'ho ka mpefala' (it could get worse). 'Le halefile' for moody is fine.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le bonahala le halefile. Ho ka mpefala.

rows.en: 50/50 on the rain. Bring a jacket, just in case.
rows.draft: 50/50 ka pula. Nka baki, e le ka mohla.
rows.reason: 'e le ka mohla' is not how anyone says 'just in case', and '50/50 ka pula' is stiff; say the rain is 50/50 and give the reason plainly.
rows.rewrite: Pula ke 50/50. Nka jase, pula e ka na.

rows.en: Some wind expected. Strength still TBC.
rows.draft: Ho lebeletsoe moea o itseng. Matla ha a e-s'o netefatsoe.
rows.reason: 'moea o itseng' (a certain wind) is the dictionary 'some', not speech; the TBC half works in bureau register, so keep it and drop 'o itseng'.
rows.rewrite: Ho lebeletswe moya. Matla a wona ha a e-so netefatswe.

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.draft: Fridge e ikutloa e futhumetse ho feta lounge kajeno.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch (fridge, lounge) and 'e ikutlwa e futhumetse' matches the confirmed 'Maoto a hao a ikutlwa eka ke ice blocks'; the cold-house joke carries.

rows.en: The world got a soft filter this morning.
rows.draft: Lefatše le fumane filitha e bonolo hoseng.
rows.reason: 'filitha' is a forced loan (people say 'filter'), 'fumane' (found) is flat, and 'hoseng' alone is 'in the morning', not 'this morning'.
rows.rewrite: Lefatshe le kentse filter e bonolo hoseng hona.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.draft: Ponelopele ea kajeno: medium rare.
rows.reason: Same shape as the confirmed 'Lehodimo la kajeno: le sa loadhella'; 'medium rare' stays as the steak code-switch, which is the joke.

rows.en: The wind has a personal vendetta against umbrellas.
rows.draft: Moea o na le vendetta ea motho ka bo eena khahlanong le disekhele.
rows.reason: 'vendetta' is not a word Sesotho speakers switch to, and 'ea motho ka bo eena' is a word-for-word calque of 'personal'; the whole line reads translated. A speaker says the wind 'has an issue with' umbrellas.
rows.rewrite: Moya o na le taba le disekhele — o di hloile ka nnete.

rows.en: Forecast: vibes neutral, expectations lower.
rows.draft: Ponelopele: vibes li bohareng, litebello li tlase.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed 'Matla a Moqebelo: a hodimo. Boikarabelo: bo tlase.'; 'vibes' code-switch and 'litebello li tlase' are natural.

rows.en: The lapa cushions are crispy.
rows.draft: Di-cushion tsa lapa di crispy.
rows.reason: 'di crispy' leaves the whole joke in an English adjective a reader may not take as sun-baked; say they are roasted by the sun ('besa', as in the confirmed steak line).
rows.rewrite: Di-cushion tsa lapa di besitswe ke letsatsi.

rows.en: Probably cold. Take the jersey, you'll thank us.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho bata. Nka jeresi, u tla re leboha.
rows.reason: Natural and warm: 'Mohlomong ho bata' matches the confirmed low-confidence lines, and 'u tla re leboha' carries 'you'll thank us'.

rows.en: Unplug the things. The sky has plans.
rows.draft: Tlosa lintho ho motlakase. Lehodimo le na le merero.
rows.reason: 'ho motlakase' should take the locative 'motlakaseng', and 'ntsha' (take out) is the everyday verb for unplugging; second beat is good.
rows.rewrite: Ntsha dintho motlakaseng. Lehodimo le na le merero.

rows.en: Reapply that sunscreen or suffer.
rows.draft: Tšoaea hape kapa o hloke.
rows.reason: 'Tšoaea' means to mark, not to apply, sunscreen is missing entirely, and 'o hloke' means 'you lack', not 'suffer'; the line says nothing the English says.
rows.rewrite: Tlotsa setlolo sa letsatsi hape, kapa o tla itshola.

rows.en: Even the shade is sweating.
rows.draft: Esita le moriti o a fufuleloa.
rows.reason: 'o a fufulelwa' is the right verb; same frame as the confirmed 'Esita le moriti o futhumetse', and the sweating shade lands.

rows.en: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.
rows.draft: Mofuta oa lehodimo o etsang hore o leboge lintho tsa mahala.
rows.reason: 'leboge' is the Setswana/Sepedi form; Sesotho is 'lebohe'. Otherwise matches the confirmed 'Mofuta wa letsatsi o etsang hore o lebale...'.
rows.rewrite: Mofuta wa lehodimo o etsang hore o lebohe dintho tsa mahala.

rows.en: Sky's grumbling. Stay close to a roof.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le a duma. Lula haufi le marulelo.
rows.reason: 'le a duma' is exactly the thunder rumble, and the second beat matches the confirmed 'Dula u le haufi le marulelo'.

rows.en: The ozone layer called. It's on leave.
rows.draft: Ozone layer e llelitse. E leaveng.
rows.reason: 'e llelitse' reads as 'cried for', not 'called' (that is 'e letsitse'), and 'E leaveng' is a garbled loan; the joke does not survive.
rows.rewrite: Ozone layer e letsitse. E re e phomolong.

rows.en: Jislaaik, stay inside!
rows.draft: Eish, dula ka hare!
rows.reason: 'Eish' is the confirmed stand-in for 'Jislaaik' and 'dula ka hare' is plain natural speech.

rows.en: Sunscreen is not optional, boet.
rows.draft: Setofo sa letsatsi ha se kgetho, boet.
rows.reason: 'Setofo' reads as stove (banned word); sunscreen is 'setlolo sa letsatsi'. The rest ('ha se kgetho, boet') is natural.
rows.rewrite: Setlolo sa letsatsi ha se kgetho, boet.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.draft: Letamo le ne le tebile ho feta kamoo le neng le shebahala kateng. Le lula le tebile.
rows.reason: Natural, correct comparative; 'letamo' for puddle is the natives' own word (confirmed heat line), and the 'always' turn reads.

rows.en: This is the stuff. Right here.
rows.draft: Ke sona sena. Mona feela.
rows.reason: 'Ke sona sena' is right, but 'Mona feela' reads 'only here'; the emphatic 'right here' is 'Hona mona'.
rows.rewrite: Ke sona sena. Hona mona.

rows.en: Probably fog later. The Boland does this.
rows.draft: Mohlomong mohodi hamorao. Boland e etsa sena.
rows.reason: Near-identical to the confirmed 'Mohlomong ho serame. Boland e etsa sena hoseng.'; 'mohodi' is the house word for fog.

rows.en: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le na le 'mala oa sekoahelo sa Tupperware sa khale.
rows.reason: Plain, natural description; Tupperware stays as the brand and the drab-lid image carries in Sesotho.

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.draft: Setulo sa koloi ea hao ke sebetsa joale.
rows.reason: 'ke sebetsa joale' can read as 'I am working now'; a speaker would say the seat has become a weapon, and 'hona jwale' for right now.
rows.rewrite: Setulo sa koloi ya hao se fetohile sebetsa hona jwale.

rows.en: Take a brolly just in case, hey.
rows.draft: Nka sekhele ho ba sireletsehile, hey.
rows.reason: 'ho ba sireletsehile' is a stiff calque of 'to be safe'; 'just in case' is said as 'in case it rains'.
rows.rewrite: Nka sekhele, hey, haeba pula e ka na.

rows.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rows.draft: 50/50 ho ba metsi. Joalo ka papadi.
rows.reason: 'Joalo ka papadi' means 'like a game' and loses the coin toss; 'ho ba metsi' is understood but a speaker says 'ho kolobela' for getting wet.
rows.rewrite: Ke 50/50 hore o tla kolobela. Jwalo ka ho flip-a coin.

rows.en: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.draft: Lena ke leholimo leo re le iponelang lichaba.
rows.reason: 're le iponelang lichaba' (we see it for ourselves the nations) is garbled; neither 'brag' nor 'overseas' comes through.
rows.rewrite: Lena ke lehodimo leo re ithorisang ka lona mose ho mawatle.

rows.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rows.draft: Maru ke karabo. Ka letšoao.
rows.reason: 'Maru ke karabo. Ka letšoao.' reads 'Clouds are the answer. With a sign.' — the asterisk/caveat joke means nothing to a reader.
rows.rewrite: Mohlomong ke maru. Ha re na bonnete ka botlalo.

rows.en: Even the Capetonians are admitting it's cold.
rows.draft: Esita le ba Cape ba lumela hore ho a bata.
rows.reason: Natural spoken shape ('ba Cape' like 'ba Joburg'); the Capetonians-admitting-it beat comes through.

rows.en: Welkom, Sasolburg, Kroonstad: the koue belt is doing its koue thing.
rows.draft: Welkom, Sasolburg, Kroonstad: koue belt e etsa koue thing ya yona.
rows.reason: 'koue belt' is the joke and can stay, but 'koue thing' leaves English carrying the sentence where Sesotho has its own words.
rows.rewrite: Welkom, Sasolburg, Kroonstad: koue belt e a bata jwalo ka mehla.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.draft: Lehodimo la Afrika le fapane feela.
rows.reason: Simple and natural; 'le fapane feela' carries 'hits different' as a warm brag.

rows.en: The sun is technically present. Spiritually elsewhere.
rows.draft: Letsatsi ka tsela ea ts'ebetso le teng. Ka moea le sebakeng se seng.
rows.reason: 'ka tsela ea ts'ebetso' (by way of operation) is a calque of 'technically'; 'ka moea' for spiritually works and should stay, set against 'ka mmele'.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le teng ka mmele. Empa ka moya, le sebakeng se seng.

rows.en: Don't touch the seatbelt buckle. Trust us.
rows.draft: Se ke oa ama buckle ea seatbelt. Re tšepe.
rows.reason: Natural imperative with car-part code-switching, and 'Re tšepe' as natives already keep it.

rows.en: Slip-slops, shorts, sun. The trinity.
rows.draft: Slip-slops, libhulukoe tse khutšoanyane, letsatsi. Boraro bo bong.
rows.reason: 'Boraro bo bong' is the established Sesotho word for the Trinity, so the joke lands exactly; the shorts phrase matches a kept line.

rows.en: Even the bakkies on the N2 pulled over.
rows.draft: Esita le li-bakkie tsa N2 li emile ka thoko.
rows.reason: 'li emile ka thoko' is the natural way to say pulled over; bakkie and N2 stay as they are.

rows.en: Protect that face! It's the only one you've got.
rows.draft: Sireletsa sefahleho seo! Ke se le seng feela o nang le sona.
rows.reason: Second beat drops the relative: 'ke se le seng feela o nang le sona' needs 'seo'; a speaker would say 'Ke sona feela seo o nang le sona'.
rows.rewrite: Sireletsa sefahleho sa hao! Ke sona feela seo o nang le sona.

rows.en: Cloud's around. How much is up for debate.
rows.draft: Maru a potolohile. Hore na a makae ke ngangisano.
rows.reason: 'a potolohile' means circling around, not 'are about'; 'a makae ke ngangisano' is stiff — speakers say 'Maru a teng' and 'we don't agree'.
rows.rewrite: Maru a teng. Hore na a mangata hakae, ha re eso dumellane.

rows.en: The sky's giving 'I'll try again tomorrow' energy.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le fana le 'ke tla leka hosane' matla.
rows.reason: 'le fana le ... matla' is a broken calque of 'giving ... energy' ('fana le' is wrong, energy is not matla here); let the sky say the line itself.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le re: 'Ke tla leka hape hosane.'

rows.en: The geyser tripped overnight. Of course it did.
rows.draft: Geyser e tripile bosiu. Of course e entse jwalo.
rows.reason: 'Geyser e tripile' is natural code-switching, but 'Of course' leaves English carrying the turn where Sesotho says 'Ehlile'.
rows.rewrite: Geyser e tripile bosiu. Ehlile e entse jwalo.

rows.en: Garage pie for lunch because the kitchen is lava.
rows.draft: Paee ea garage hobane kitchen ke lava.
rows.reason: Drops 'for lunch'; 'Paee' is an odd spelling of the loan (phae/pie) and 'kitchen' is left English where 'kitjhene' is the everyday word.
rows.rewrite: Pie ya garage motsheare, hobane kitjhene ke lava.

rows.en: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.
rows.draft: Palo ea kofi: e nyolohang. Palo ea khothatso: e ntse e le zero.
rows.reason: 'e nyolohang' is a dangling relative ('which is rising'); the label shape needs the predicate 'e a nyoloha'.
rows.rewrite: Palo ya kofi: e a nyoloha. Palo ya kgothatso: e ntse e le zero.

rows.en: Even your GPS is confused.
rows.draft: Esita le GPS ea hao e ferekane.
rows.reason: Natural, same shape as the kept Google Maps line; 'e ferekane' is exactly right.

rows.en: Your nose is going to betray you by 3pm.
rows.draft: Nko ea hao e tla o eka ka 3pm.
rows.reason: 'e tla o eka' uses betray as natives already keep it; 3pm code-switched naturally.

rows.en: The sun's on a tea break. No ETA.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le phomoletseng ho noa tee. Ha ho ETA.
rows.reason: 'le phomoletseng' is a dangling relative and 'phomoletse ho noa tee' is stiff; the kept line says 'Letsatsi le nka kgefu'.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le nka kgefu ya tee. Ha ho ETA.

rows.en: The vibe is beige. Accept it.
rows.draft: Vibe ke beige. Amohela.
rows.reason: 'Amohela' alone is bare; 'accept it' needs the object, 'E amohele'.
rows.rewrite: Vibe ke beige. E amohele feela.
